finding: §4.6.5 deadlocks every PR whose intent axis is unavailable. It says `cr review <pr>` "MUST then refuse to emit prompts for the remaining axes until `mapping.ndjson` exists, with exit code 4", and the only producer of that file is the intent role emitted by `cr review <pr> --axis intent`. But §3.2 says that when no key is found "`cr` MUST continue with an empty intent and mark the intent axis unavailable per §4.5", and §4.5.3 confirms the axis is unavailable. An unavailable axis has no active role, so no intent prompt is emitted, so `mapping.ndjson` never comes into existence, so `cr review` exits 4 forever — the correctness, convention and test axes become unreachable on any PR without a tracker key. Two engineers write opposite tests here: `TestReview_NoIssueKey_EmitsRemainingAxes` versus `TestReview_NoMapping_Exit4`.
suggestion: State the exception explicitly: when the intent axis is unavailable per §4.5.3, `cr` MUST treat the mapping as empty-by-construction, write an empty `mapping.ndjson` (or record the unavailability in `meta.json`), and emit the remaining axes' prompts with every unit marked unmapped-because-no-intent rather than exiting 4.

finding: The gap probe has no baseline guard, so a pre-existing suite failure manufactures a `probed`, severity-high assertion. §5.2.2 states the rationale — a baseline is recorded "so pre-existing failures are never attributed to a probe" — but §5.5's table marks `baseline` "required for a `mutation` probe" only, and §5.4.3/§5.4.4 never mention it. §5.4.3 rung 6 is "otherwise → `failed`", i.e. failed count > 0 over whatever the run selected, and `--filter` is optional (§5.5 lists `filter` as not required). So on a repository with one already-red test, an unfiltered gap probe returns `failed`, §5.4.4 grants it `probed` and "Severity MUST be at least `high`" the moment the agent sets `claim`. A test asserting `TestGapProbe_PreExistingFailure_DoesNotSupportFinding` has nothing in the spec to assert against, and the spec's own §5.3.5 protection has no counterpart here.
suggestion: Make `baseline` required for `gap` probes too, and add to §5.4.4: a `failed` gap probe supports the finding only when the baseline matching this probe's filter passed and the baseline's failed count is strictly less than the probe run's, otherwise the result MUST be recorded as `inconclusive` and MUST NOT support a `probed` grade.

finding: §9.1's transition table is declared closed — "Transitions are exhaustive. A transition not listed here MUST be rejected with exit code 4" — and the only edge into `posted` is "`queued` | `posted` | `cr post --confirm`". But §8.4.4 requires `cr post <pr> --reconcile` to "either adopt that review as posted or clear the state for a retry". `--reconcile` is a distinct invocation in §11 (`cr post <pr> [--confirm] [--reconcile]`) and performs no network write, so §8.5.2 does not force `--confirm` onto it. Implementing §8.4.4 literally means performing a `queued`→`posted` transition from a command the exhaustive table does not name, which §9.1 orders rejected with exit 4. The recovery path for the one failure mode §8.4 exists to handle is therefore unreachable, and there is no way to reconcile a review that GitHub actually created. "Clear the state for a retry" is equally undefined: no state was set to clear, since §8.4.2 only forbids marking posted.
suggestion: Add the reconcile edges to the §9.1 table: `queued` → `posted` produced by `cr post --reconcile` (adopt), and state the retry branch as a no-op on record state. State whether `--reconcile` requires `--confirm`; if adoption is a state write rather than a network write, say so explicitly so §8.5.2 is not read as gating it.

finding: The scope cut leaves v0.1 with no way to stop a second round from re-asserting a concern the author has already answered. §9.3.3 says "findings, units, cells, and probes MUST NOT [carry into a new round], because each is bound to a head", and §1.3.6 defers "verifying that a concern was addressed, resolving threads, and withdrawing a posted concern" to v0.2. So round 2 re-derives and re-posts every finding the author has not fixed — including one the author refuted in a reply. The only defence is §3.5.4's agent judgement, and it is reachable only through §3.5.3, which attaches "ingested human threads whose anchor falls inside the unit's hunks or within `threads.proximity_lines`". §9.2.2 forbids anchor migration in v0.1, so a thread on code the author edited in response — the single most likely case after a review — has no resolvable line at the new head, and §3.5 says nothing about what happens to such a thread. Nothing tags an ingested thread as cr's own prior comment either: §3.5.2 tags only `human` or `bot`, and §9.3.3 discards the `thread_id` that would identify it. Re-asserting a refuted claim on a colleague's PR is the most expensive act in this trust economy, and v0.1 has no mechanism against it — only luck.
suggestion: Carry a head-independent index of the previous round's posted records into the new round, keyed exactly like a §7.4.1 waiver — (anchor.path, class, rule id when present, normalised hash of the anchored lines) — plus the `thread_id`, and require `cr` to attach any match to the unit as an explicit suppression candidate the way §3.5.3 attaches threads. Require §3.5 to report every ingested thread whose anchor no longer resolves as an `outdated` set rather than dropping it silently. Add to §13.1 that v0.1 re-raises anything not fixed, so the reviewer knows the second round needs a manual pass before `--confirm`.

finding: §9.3.3 says that on a new round "findings, units, cells, and probes MUST NOT [carry into it], because each is bound to a head", but no mechanism is defined and the surrounding schema assumes the opposite. §2.3 gives one flat `findings.ndjson` holding "All findings and questions, all states"; §6.1 makes `id` "`f<n>`, stable for the life of the PR" and carries `round`, `head`, and `thread_id`. A round-1 record in state `posted` with a live `thread_id` cannot be dropped without losing the PR's posting history, yet it plainly "carries into" round 2 under any reading. Worse, a record left in `draft` when the head moves is trapped: §9.1's table exits `draft` only to `duplicate`/`suppressed` (`cr record`) or `queued` (`cr draft`), and §9.3.2 refuses `cr draft` outright once the heads differ. There is no `draft`→`discarded` edge, so the record can never reach a terminal state and §10.2.4 ("No record remains in `draft` or `queued`") is unsatisfiable for that PR forever. An implementer must invent both a per-round partitioning scheme and a stranded-record escape.
suggestion: Say precisely what happens to each per-PR file when the head moves: keep `findings.ndjson` append-only and scope every round's queries by the `round`/`head` fields (recommended, since it preserves `thread_id` and id stability), rather than saying records "MUST NOT carry into" the round. Add a `draft`→`discarded` transition (or an automatic `stale` terminal state) produced by whatever command opens the new round, so no record is stranded at a dead head.

finding: "Active role" carries a completeness verdict and an exit code and is defined nowhere. §10.2.2 requires "a complete row of cells for every active role"; §4.5.6 says `cr` "MUST reject with exit code 1 a cell naming an unknown unit id or an inactive role"; §4.6.1 emits prompts "For every active role". §4.5.1 defines activation for an *axis*, not a role, and §2.5.6 adds an orthogonal `profiles` scope while §4.6.4 introduces a third status, "skipped", with no statement of whether a skipped role remains active. Three readings — axis active; axis active and profile matches; axis active, profile matches, and not skipped — give three different answers to `TestCellsRecord_RejectsInactiveRole` and three different completeness verdicts for the same state directory.
suggestion: Define it in §4.5: a role is active when its `axis` is active per §4.5.1, its `profiles` list is empty or contains the resolved profile, and it was not reported skipped per §4.6.4; state that the set of active roles is recorded in `meta.json` for the round so §4.5.6 and §10.2.2 read the same set.

finding: The only escape from §10.2.3's block has no command behind it. §10.2.3 says an unimplemented claim "MUST block completeness until it is either mapped, or set aside by a note per §3.6 naming it out of scope for this pull request", and §4.1.3 gives the entry a `set_aside_note` field "when §10.2.3 applies". Nothing writes that field: §11 lists `cr note <ISSUE-KEY> <text>`, which takes an issue key and no claim id and appends to `~/.cr/context/<ISSUE-KEY>.ndjson`, and `cr answer <pr> <record-id>` which needs a record id an intent gap is explicitly forbidden from having. `cr` also cannot infer the link, since §4.1.5 forbids it deciding "by matching text". So a PR that legitimately implements only part of an issue can never be reported complete, and `TestCompleteness_ClaimSetAside` cannot be set up at all.
suggestion: Add the write path to §11 and §4.1.3 — e.g. `cr claims set-aside <pr> <claim-id> --note <note-id>`, which validates that the note exists for the PR's issue key, stamps `set_aside_note` on the `intent-gaps.ndjson` entry, and records the round and head.

finding: §10.2.3 makes an unimplemented claim block completeness "until it is either mapped, or set aside by a note per §3.6 naming it out of scope for this pull request", and §4.1.3 stores `set_aside_note` on the `intent-gaps.ndjson` entry "when §10.2.3 applies". Nothing writes that field and nobody is assigned the judgement. §11's command table has no command that binds a note to a claim: `cr note <ISSUE-KEY> <text>` records against an issue key, and §3.6 never mentions claims or gap entries. That leaves the sole release valve on a blocking condition unreachable, and it puts implementation pressure exactly where the spec elsewhere forbids it — deciding that a note "names it out of scope" is text matching, which §4.1.5 explicitly denies `cr` for the analogous case ("`cr` MUST NOT decide this by matching text"), and it is absent from §2.1.3's enumeration of judgements reserved to the agent. Either completeness is permanently unattainable whenever a claim is genuinely out of scope, teaching the reviewer to ignore the verdict, or `cr` starts forming the opinion P5 forbids.
suggestion: Add an explicit agent-driven command — e.g. `cr claims set-aside <pr> <claim-id> --note <note-id> --reason <text>` — that validates the note exists for the issue key and writes `set_aside_note` on the gap entry, and list it in §11. State in §10.2.3 that the set-aside is the agent's judgement recorded by `cr`, never a match `cr` performs, and add it to §2.1.3's list. Require `cr status` to show set-aside claims with their note id so the exemption stays visible rather than disappearing from the report.

finding: `mapping.ndjson` is head-bound in effect but head-less in the schema, so a stale mapping silently passes the new two-pass gate. §2.3.3 requires a `head` field only on "`claims.ndjson`, `units.ndjson`, `findings.ndjson`, `probes.ndjson`, and `coverage.ndjson`" — the mapping is excluded, and §4.1.6 defines its lines as "one `{claim, unit}` pair per line" with no head or round. §9.3.3's must-not-carry list is "findings, units, cells, and probes" and also omits it. After a head change the old mapping survives, referencing unit ids the new clustering need not reproduce (§3.4.6 reuses an id only when "file path set and unit hash are both unchanged"), and it satisfies §4.6.5's gate verbatim: `cr review` refuses "until `mapping.ndjson` exists". The gate added to prevent "emitting prompts with an empty mapping" therefore passes on a wrong one, which is worse — every downstream axis reads claims for units they do not belong to.
suggestion: Add `head` and `round` to mapping rows, list `mapping.ndjson` in §2.3.3 and in §9.3.3's must-not-carry set, and change §4.6.5's gate from existence to "a mapping whose head equals the current head and whose unit ids all exist in the current `units.ndjson`".

finding: §2.6.1 defines a three-layer rule resolution — "Rules MUST resolve in layers, highest first: per-repository, then global, then the profile's built-in rules" — but the third layer has no storage anywhere. §2.2 lists only `~/.cr/rules/<id>.json` ("Global rules") and `~/.cr/repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/<id>.json` ("Per-repository rule overrides"). §2.4's profile schema has no rules field of any kind, so a profile file cannot carry rules, and unlike roles there is no `cr init --eject-rules` counterpart to §2.5.2 that would materialise built-ins as editable files. §2.6.2's "A rule id MUST be unique after resolution; a lower layer carrying the same id is overridden whole" therefore has an unimplementable bottom layer, and §11's `cr rules list --repo <owner/repo>` ("Effective rules and the layer each came from") cannot name a layer whose contents are undefined.
suggestion: Either add a `rules` array to the §2.4 profile schema and say built-in profile rules ship inside the profile file, or drop the third layer from §2.6.1 and make the built-in corpus the shipped contents of `~/.cr/rules/` written by `cr init`. Whichever is chosen, say what v0.1's built-in rule set is, as §2.4.5 does for profiles and §2.5.1 for roles.

finding: "Changed line" is load-bearing four times in §3.4 and defined nowhere, and no default side is fixed the way §2.6.1.1 fixes one for detection ("the added and modified `RIGHT`-side lines of the diff only"). §3.4.4 measures adjacency between "the last changed line of one and the first changed line of the next"; §3.4.5 splits on "`cluster.max_lines` changed lines"; §3.4.6 records "its changed line count" and "a normalised hash of its changed lines". One engineer counts RIGHT-side additions only, another counts both `+` and `-` lines, a third counts a modified line twice. They disagree on which clusters exceed 80 lines, on which units are flagged `oversized` (a §10.1.1 output), and on every unit hash — and for a deletion-only hunk the first engineer's unit hash is the hash of the empty string, which collides with every other deletion-only unit.
suggestion: Add to §3.4: a changed line is an added or modified `RIGHT`-side line, plus removed `LEFT`-side lines for a hunk that adds none; the adjacency gap of §3.4.4 is measured in `RIGHT`-side line numbers; the unit hash of §3.4.6 is the normalised hash of those lines each prefixed by `<path>:<side>:` and joined by LF, in diff order.

finding: §3.4.5's split rule admits several distinct outputs: "A cluster exceeding `cluster.max_lines` changed lines (default 80) MUST be split at hunk boundaries into the fewest units that each stay within the limit." Minimising the number of parts does not determine the partition. With hunks of 50, 30 and 50 changed lines and a limit of 80, both {50,30}+{50} and {50}+{30,50} are minimal, and the spec picks neither; worse, it does not say the parts must be contiguous, so an implementer may group non-adjacent hunks and reach the same minimum by a different route. Because unit membership determines the unit hash and hence the id, two conforming implementations produce different unit sets, different coverage rows, and different `oversized` flags for the same diff.
suggestion: Replace "the fewest units" with a deterministic greedy rule: process hunks in ascending start order and open a new unit whenever adding the next hunk would exceed `cluster.max_lines`; state that units are contiguous in hunk order.

finding: §3.4.6 and §9.3.3 contradict each other on whether units survive a round boundary, and only one of them can be tested. §3.4.6 requires that "An `id` MUST be reused across rounds for a unit whose file path set and unit hash are both unchanged", which forces `cr brief` at the new head to read the previous round's `units.ndjson`. §9.3.3 says of a new round that "findings, units, cells, and probes MUST NOT [carry into it], because each is bound to a head." §3.4.6's stated justification — "§10.2.2 needs both, and they must agree" — no longer holds either: after the v0.2 scope cut §10.2 evaluates a single round, condition 2 compares a cell to "that unit's current unit hash" within the same head, and nothing in §10.2 reads a prior round.
suggestion: Pick one. Either delete the cross-round reuse requirement from §3.4.6 (unit ids become round-scoped, matching §9.3.3) and drop the §10.2.2 justification, or carve out an explicit exception in §9.3.3 that the previous round's `units.ndjson` MAY be read for id assignment only, and say which round's file is authoritative.

finding: §3.4.6's identity key is not unique, so id reuse is not a function. It says "An `id` MUST be reused across rounds for a unit whose file path set and unit hash are both unchanged". Clustering in §3.4.4 is always within one file, so the file path set is always a singleton, and the key degenerates to (file, unit hash). Two units in the same file whose changed lines are byte-identical after §1.4 normalisation — the ordinary case of the same one-line change made in two places, or two identical guard clauses — produce the same key, and the spec gives no rule for which of them keeps `u3`. §10.2.2 then compares cells against "that unit's current unit hash", so the ambiguity propagates into the completeness verdict. `TestUnitIds_StableAcrossRounds` has two admissible expected outputs.
suggestion: Add an ordinal to the key: reuse an id for the unit whose (file path set, unit hash, index among same-key units in ascending first-hunk-start order) is unchanged, and state that when the count of same-key units changes, the surplus units get fresh ids.

finding: The three agent-input commands do not say whether a call appends or replaces, or what a second call does. §4.1.6: "`cr map record <pr> <file.ndjson>` MUST validate and store it in `mapping.ndjson`"; §4.5.6: cells "reach `cr` the same way findings do, through `cr cells record <pr> <file.ndjson>`, which validates and stores them"; §3.3.1: "`cr claims record <pr> <file.ndjson>` MUST validate and store claims". Cells must accumulate, since §4.6.1 fans out one prompt per role per unit and each role returns its own file — so `cr cells record` has to append. But then a re-run of a single role produces two cells for the same `(unit, role)` and nothing says which wins, while §10.2.2 requires "a complete row of cells" per unit. The mapping has the opposite problem: §4.6.5 has plain `cr review <pr>` emit prompts for the remaining axes once `mapping.ndjson` exists, which re-runs the intent role, and a second `cr map record` with a partial file either duplicates pairs (making a claim look mapped twice) or truncates the mapping (making units look unmapped). §3.3.3 hints claims replace — "re-extraction happens only through a new `cr claims record`" — but never says the file is truncated, nor what becomes of a `mapping.ndjson` that references claim ids the replacement dropped.
suggestion: For each of the three commands state the write mode and the idempotency key explicitly: `cr claims record` replaces `claims.ndjson` wholesale and MUST invalidate `mapping.ndjson` and `intent-gaps.ndjson`; `cr map record` replaces `mapping.ndjson` wholesale; `cr cells record` upserts by `(unit, role)` so a re-run of one role overwrites only its own cells. Name the exit code for a store that would orphan a downstream reference.

finding: `intent-gaps.ndjson` has no writer and its `set_aside_note` field has no input path. §4.1.3 says an unimplemented claim "MUST instead be written to `intent-gaps.ndjson` carrying `claim`, `round`, `head`, and `set_aside_note` when §10.2.3 applies", but no command in §11 writes the file — `cr map record` is defined only as storing `mapping.ndjson`, and the file appears nowhere else in the document except the §2.3 table. More seriously, §10.2.3 makes the entry block completeness "until it is either mapped, or set aside by a note per §3.6 naming it out of scope for this pull request", yet §3.6.1's signature is `cr note <ISSUE-KEY> "<text>" --source <source>` with no way to name a claim, and deciding that a note's prose "names it out of scope" is exactly the text-matching judgement §4.1.5 forbids `cr` from making. The escape hatch is therefore unreachable: a claim genuinely out of scope for this PR blocks completeness permanently, with no command that can write `set_aside_note`.
suggestion: Name the writer — state that `cr map record` derives `intent-gaps.ndjson` from `claims.ndjson` minus `mapping.ndjson` on every successful store — and add an explicit set-aside verb, e.g. `cr map set-aside <pr> <claim-id> --note <note-id>`, that validates the note exists and writes `set_aside_note`. That keeps the judgement with the agent and the recording with `cr`, per P5.

finding: `intent-gaps.ndjson` and `set_aside_note` have no writer, and setting the latter needs a judgement `cr` is forbidden to make. §4.1.3 requires the entry to be "written to `intent-gaps.ndjson` carrying `claim`, `round`, `head`, and `set_aside_note` when §10.2.3 applies", and §10.2.3 makes that note the sole way an unimplemented claim stops blocking: it "MUST block completeness until it is either mapped, or set aside by a note per §3.6 naming it out of scope for this pull request". No command in §11 writes either file or field — `cr map record` (§4.1.6) stores only "one `{claim, unit}` pair per line". Deciding that a note names a claim out of scope is a text judgement of exactly the kind §4.1.5 forbids ("`cr` MUST NOT decide this by matching text") and §2.1.3 reserves to the agent. Completeness is therefore unreachable for a claim that is genuinely out of scope. This is the same defect class as the mapping's missing writer, repaired in round 4.
suggestion: Name the writer: derive the gap entries mechanically inside `cr map record` from claims mapped to zero units, and add an explicit judgement command (e.g. `cr intent-gaps set-aside <pr> <claim-id> --note <note-id>`) or an optional per-claim `set_aside_note` in `cr map record`'s input.

finding: §4.3.1 requires `cr` to "search the repository for candidate pre-existing symbols", and the universe of that search is never fixed: symbols indexed at the merge base, or at the head minus the symbols the diff added, or at the head unfiltered. The ranking of §4.3.2 is otherwise fully deterministic, which makes the omission the only source of divergence — and it is a large one. Indexed at the head unfiltered, every added symbol matches itself at similarity 1.0 with an equal parameter count and becomes its own reinvention candidate. Indexed at the merge base, a renamed function matches its own former name at high similarity with an identical parameter count, and §4.3.4 posts a question to the author about the symbol they just renamed — a false positive of exactly the kind §1.6 says spends trust.
suggestion: State the universe in §4.3.1: candidates are the symbols present in the head index minus every symbol declared by an added or modified `RIGHT`-side line of the diff, and minus any symbol whose declaration site is inside the record's own unit. Add a worked example so the self-match and rename cases are pinned.

finding: `mapping.ndjson` is the one judgement-bearing state file with no head stamp and no clearing rule. §2.3.3 stamps only "`claims.ndjson`, `units.ndjson`, `findings.ndjson`, `probes.ndjson`, and `coverage.ndjson`"; §9.3.3 clears only "findings, units, cells, and probes"; §4.6.5 gates every remaining axis on existence alone — "MUST then refuse to emit prompts for the remaining axes until `mapping.ndjson` exists, with exit code 4". A mapping produced at head A therefore survives a head change, satisfies the gate at head B, and carries no field by which its staleness could even be detected. Unit ids are stable only for a unit "whose file path set and unit hash are both unchanged" (§3.4.6), so after a push a surviving mapping silently re-points `u<n>` at different code. §4.2.1 then evaluates each unit "against the claims it is mapped to" and §4.2.2 requires "A correctness finding MUST cite the claim id it violates" — putting a confidently wrong claim id in front of the author. §4.6.5's own stated purpose is to prevent "emitting prompts with an empty mapping"; a stale mapping is worse than an empty one, because it looks right.
suggestion: Add `mapping.ndjson` to §2.3.3's head-stamped set and to §9.3.3's list of state that MUST NOT carry into a new round. Change §4.6.5's gate from existence to freshness: refuse unless the mapping's head equals the current head, with exit code 4 naming both heads and hinting at `cr map record`.

finding: §5.3.5 gates the only grade a mutation probe can produce on a property run records do not have: "Only `no-test-failed` proves the gap, and only when the baseline matching this probe's filter passed." The run-record schema of §5.2.4 carries `id`, `head`, `filter`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `tests_run` and `tests_failed` "when derivable", and `output_tail` — there is no verdict field and no rule turning those into passed/not-passed. Since §5.2.1 says an unmatched `tests.count_pattern` "leaves both counts undetermined", a baseline on a profile with no count pattern has neither counts nor a verdict, and `cr` cannot evaluate §5.3.5 at all. Separately, nothing provisions the baseline: `cr probe run <pr> --kind mutation --patch <file> --filter <expr>` (§5.3.2) has no `--baseline` flag, while §5.5 marks `baseline` "required for a `mutation` probe | Id of the run record (§5.2.4) whose filter matches this probe's". If no run record matches the probe's filter — the normal case on a first probe — the spec says neither that `cr` runs one automatically nor that it aborts.
suggestion: Add a `passed` boolean (or a `result` field on the same ladder shape as §5.3.4) to the §5.2.4 run record and define it — e.g. passed iff `exit_code == 0` and, when derivable, `tests_failed == 0` — then have §5.3.5 refer to that field. State the missing-baseline behaviour in §5.3.2: `cr probe run --kind mutation` MUST record the matching baseline itself before applying the mutation, or MUST abort with exit code 4 naming the filter.

finding: §5.3.5 gates the only path to a `probed` grade on a predicate that does not exist: "only when the baseline matching this probe's filter passed". Run records are defined in §5.2.4 and carry `id`, `head`, `filter`, `exit_code`, `duration_ms`, `tests_run`, `tests_failed`, `output_tail` — there is no `result` field and no definition of a run "passing". §5.5's per-kind result vocabulary is explicitly for probes. One engineer implements `exit_code == 0`, another `tests_failed == 0`, and they disagree on every runner that exits 0 while reporting failures in text, and on every profile with no `tests.count_pattern` (where `tests_failed` is undetermined and the predicate has no truth value at all).
suggestion: Define baseline pass in §5.2.4: a run record passes when `exit_code == 0` AND, when `tests.count_pattern` is configured and matched, `tests_failed == 0`. State what happens when the counts are undetermined — recommended: the baseline is not passing, so the probe MUST NOT support a `probed` grade, matching the `inconclusive` rung's intent.

finding: `probe.test_dir`'s default is "the root of the first entry in the profile's `tests.globs`" (§5.4.2, repeated in §2.4), and "root" of a glob is defined nowhere. For `tests/**/*Test.php` one engineer takes `tests` (longest wildcard-free directory prefix), another takes `tests` only if they special-case `**`; for `**/*_test.go` the first reads the repository root and the second reads `**`; for `{tests,spec}/**/*.php` neither has a rule. The same undefined term also decides which directory §5.1.6 scans for leftover artefacts, so the cleanliness check and the placement can disagree.
suggestion: Define it mechanically: the default `probe.test_dir` is the longest leading path prefix of the first `tests.globs` entry that contains no glob metacharacter (`*`, `?`, `[`, `{`); when that prefix is empty the profile MUST declare `probe.test_dir` explicitly or the gap probe aborts with exit code 3 naming the profile.

finding: §5.4.2's literal filename cannot satisfy the test-file patterns of the profile that supplies `probe.test_dir`. The probe file MUST be "named exactly `cr_probe_<probe-id>` plus the extension of the supplied file", placed at the root derived from `tests.globs`, whose §2.4 meaning is "Patterns identifying test files". For the `laravel-pest` profile §2.4.5 mandates, that pattern is of the form `tests/**/*Test.php`, which `tests/cr_probe_p1.php` does not match, so the runner never collects the probe test: the executed count is zero and §5.4.3 rung 3 returns `no-tests-selected` for every gap probe, which §5.4.5 says "prove[s] nothing". The gap probe is inoperable on one of the two shipped profiles, and `TestGapProbe_ShippedProfile_Passed` cannot be made to pass.
suggestion: Derive the probe filename from the profile instead of pinning it globally: add a `tests.probe_name_template` (or require the name to be the first `tests.globs` entry with its wildcard segment replaced by `cr_probe_<probe-id>`), keep `cr_probe_` as the mandatory prefix so §5.1.6's cleanliness check still recognises the artefact, and state that the resulting name MUST match at least one `tests.globs` entry or the command aborts with exit code 3.

finding: `target` is a required probe-record field with no defined source for either kind. §5.5's table demands `target` = "`path:line` the probe addresses", but the invocations of §5.3.2 and §5.4.2 are `cr probe run <pr> --kind mutation --patch <file> --filter <expr>` and `cr probe run <pr> --kind gap --test <file> --filter <expr>` — neither takes a target, and §11's row is only `cr probe run <pr> --kind <kind> ...`. For a mutation, the patch may touch several files and several hunks and the spec does not say which one becomes the target; for a gap probe the input is a brand-new test file, so no target is derivable from the inputs at all. Since §6.2.1 says grading's "only inputs are `citations` and the referenced probe record", a required field of that record is left to each implementer to invent.
suggestion: Add an explicit `--target <path:line>` flag to `cr probe run`, required for both kinds, validated against the current head exactly as §6.2.3 validates a citation; or, for mutations only, define it as the first changed `RIGHT`-side line of the first file in the supplied patch and say so.

finding: `state` is agent-writable, which contradicts cr's ownership of the state machine. The schema marks `| `state` | yes | State per §9.1 |` — required, not computed — and §6.1.4's forbidden list is "`grade`, `span_hash`, `issue_hash`, a citation's `content_hash` or `origin`, or any other field marked computed". Nothing stops a role from writing `state: posted`, `state: discarded`, `duplicate_of`, or `thread_id`, and §9.1's exhaustive transition table would then be enforced against a value the agent chose. It also makes two rows of that table fictional: §3.5.4 requires a thread-suppressed finding to "be recorded in state `suppressed`" at creation and §6.4.3 the same for `duplicate`, so neither record was ever in `draft`, yet the table gives `draft` as their only origin.
suggestion: Mark `state`, `disposition`, `duplicate_of`, and `thread_id` computed in §6.1 and add them to §6.1.4's rejection list; restate the entry rows of §9.1 as `—`→`draft`, `—`→`duplicate`, `—`→`suppressed` at `cr record`, driven by the agent-supplied `duplicate_of`/`suppressed_by` rather than by an agent-supplied `state`.

finding: The waiver key is narrower than the dedup key, so a rejected finding resurfaces by changing producer. §7.4.1 keys a waiver by "(anchor.path, class, rule id when present, normalised hash of the anchored lines)"; §6.4.1 dedups by "(anchor.path, anchor.line, class)" with no rule id. Two records that §6.4 collapses into one therefore waive to two distinct keys. Concretely: the reviewer marks a rule-produced record `disposition=wrong`, which §7.2 says writes a repository-wide waiver; next round the identical class at identical unchanged code arrives from a role that carries no `rule` field, misses the key, and is posted again — after the reviewer has already told the tool it is false. §7.4.2 states the intent the key does not deliver: "It suppresses the same class at the same unchanged code in the same file." And §7.4.6 already gives rules their own scoping lever — "A waiver for a record produced by a rule MAY be widened to a path prefix" — so the rule id buys nothing in the key while opening this hole.
suggestion: Drop `rule id` from §7.4.1's key, leaving `(anchor.path, class, normalised hash of the anchored lines)` so it matches the class-based identity §6.4.1 already uses. Keep the rule id as a recorded field on the waiver for §7.3's per-rule statistics and for §7.4.6's path-prefix widening, and say explicitly that a waiver written for a rule-produced record also suppresses the same class at the same code from any other producer.

finding: §8.1.7 requires `cr` to "append its own citation block beneath the agent-written body of every `cited` record", defending it as "unlike a rule addressed to the agent it is something `cr` can actually enforce" — but nothing in the spec puts it beyond the reach of the two parties who own the body. §8.1.2: "The agent then rewrites that body in `render.lang` by editing `draft.md`." §7.1.2: "The block body MUST be free-form Markdown that the user may rewrite entirely." §2.7's protected set is "the confirmation gate of §8.5, the argued forcing of §6.3, and the question label of §8.1.4" and does not include §8.1.7. §8.1.4's label survives because it is `cr`-owned and named in §2.7; §8.1.7's block is described only as appended, with no statement of when it is produced relative to the edit cycle and no rule that it is regenerated or that its removal is rejected. Deleting it is therefore just "Posted as edited" under §7.2, and the assertion reaches the author with the one location that warranted it stripped off — the exact failure §8.1.7 closes with ("posting the assertion while withholding the location asks the author to take it on trust").
suggestion: State in §8.1.7 that the citation block is `cr`-owned and generated by template substitution from the record's stored `citations`, that it is regenerated at render time and again immediately before the payload is built (the same belt-and-braces as §6.3.1), that it is excluded from the editable body for the purposes of §7.1.5's edit detection and §7.2's edit semantics, and add §8.1.7 to §2.7's list of things no layer may address.

finding: A multi-line anchor cannot survive to a posted comment. §9.2 requires every anchor to carry `start_line` and `line`, and §9.2's content hash is defined over "the lines from `start_line` to `line` inclusive", so multi-line records are a first-class case. But `start_line` appears nowhere downstream: §7.1.1's draft marker carries only "`id`, `kind`, `path`, `line`, `severity`, `grade`, and `disposition`", §7.2's marker edit table validates only "`path`, `line`", and §8.3.3's payload pre-image is "each comment contributes its `path`, `line`, `side`, and `body` joined by LF, in that order". Two consequences: a multi-line GitHub comment (which requires `start_line`) cannot be expressed in the payload the spec specifies, which also breaks §8.2.1's "A suggestion MUST map to a contiguous line range" for any range longer than one line; and two comments differing only in `start_line` produce the same payload hash, so §8.4.4's reconcile can match the wrong review.
suggestion: Add `start_line` to the §7.1.1 marker fields and to §7.2's re-validated fields, and insert it into §8.3.3's pre-image (`path`, `start_line`, `line`, `side`, `body`), with an explicit rendering — e.g. the empty string — when the anchor is single-line, so the pre-image stays unambiguous.

finding: §8.3.3's pre-image ordering has no tiebreak, so the payload hash is not a function of the payload. It says "the comments are ordered by `path` ascending then `line` ascending". Two comments can share both: §6.4.1 deduplicates by `(anchor.path, anchor.line, class)`, so two records of different classes at the same anchor both survive and both post. Their relative order then falls to map or slice iteration order, and the hash differs between runs of the same binary on the same state. That defeats the recovery path of §8.4.4, which matches "the embedded payload hash of §8.4.3" to decide whether to "adopt that review as posted or clear the state for a retry" — a missed match clears the state and the round is posted twice, which §8.4.4 itself calls "a worse failure than posting late". It also breaks §2.1.1's reproducibility requirement.
suggestion: Extend the ordering to a total one: by `path` ascending, then `line` ascending, then `side` ascending (`LEFT` before `RIGHT`), then the record id ascending by its numeric suffix. State that the ordering must be total and give the tiebreak explicitly.

finding: §8.4.4 makes `cr post <pr> --reconcile` the only exit from a `post-unresolved` round, justified as "Posting twice is a worse failure than posting late." §9.3.2 then disables it: "When they differ, `cr` MUST refuse to draft, post, or probe, with exit code 4" — and `cr post --reconcile` is `cr post`. The head moving is precisely what a posted review provokes, so the escape hatch is unavailable exactly when it is needed. The round stays `post-unresolved`, §9.3.3 forces a fresh round that drops the findings and their `thread_id`s, and the same comments are posted a second time: the outcome §8.4.4 names as the worse failure. Compounding it, `post-unresolved` has no home in §2.3, no state in §9.1's six-state table, and no transition out of `queued` — yet §9.1 declares "Transitions are exhaustive. A transition not listed here MUST be rejected with exit code 4."
suggestion: Exempt `cr post --reconcile` from §9.3.2's refusal and say why: it anchors nothing and only matches the §8.4.3 payload hash against the PR's existing reviews, so a moved head cannot affect its correctness. Require that a PR whose last round is `post-unresolved` be reconciled before §9.3.3 permits a new round. Give `post-unresolved` a storage location in §2.3 and name the `queued`→`posted` transition reconciliation produces in §9.1's table.

finding: The exhaustive transition table omits the reconcile path. §8.4.4 requires that `cr post <pr> --reconcile` "match the embedded payload hash of §8.4.3, and either adopt that review as posted or clear the state for a retry". Adopting is a `queued`→`posted` transition, but the table lists that transition only for `cr post --confirm`, and the table's preamble requires any unlisted transition to "be rejected with exit code 4" — so §9.1 as written forbids the recovery §8.4 mandates. §8.4.4 also requires `cr` to "mark the round `post-unresolved`", a round-level state §9.1 does not define, §2.3 provides no file or `meta.json` field for, and whose "clear the state for a retry" names no state either.
suggestion: Add `cr post --reconcile` to the command column of the `queued`→`posted` row, and define `post-unresolved` as a round-level flag with a named storage location (a `meta.json` field or `rounds/<n>/posted.json` key) and an explicit clearing rule.

finding: §9.2 defines two anchor sides — "Valid `side` values are `RIGHT` and `LEFT`" and §9.2.1 "`LEFT` anchors a removed line and MUST be used only for records about deletions" — but two other MUSTs make a LEFT anchor impossible to carry. §6.1.2: "Every record MUST carry an anchor that resolves to a line in the current head." A removed line by definition does not exist in the head. §7.2's marker table repeats it: "`path`, `line` | Re-validated against the current head; aborts when the anchor no longer resolves." So every LEFT-anchored record is rejected at record time by §6.1.2 and aborts triage at §7.2. The same collision hits §9.2's content hash, which is "the normalised hash per §1.4 of the lines from `start_line` to `line` inclusive" without naming which file version those lines are read from — for LEFT it can only be the merge base. Either LEFT is dead machinery left over from the scope cut, or §6.1.2 and §7.2 are wrong; an implementer cannot tell which.
suggestion: Make the side explicit in the resolution rules: §6.1.2 and §7.2 should read "resolves against the head for `side: RIGHT` and against the merge base for `side: LEFT`", and §9.2 should name the file version the content hash is computed over per side. If LEFT is not actually needed in v0.1, delete it from the valid-side list and say deletions are anchored to the adjacent RIGHT line.

finding: Nothing defines when the round index advances. §9.3.3 says "A new round MUST be started by re-running `cr brief` against the new head", while §3.7 says `cr brief` "is safe to run at any point in a round" — so the same command both starts a round and is explicitly safe to repeat inside one, and no rule says whether a same-head `cr brief` increments `meta.json`'s "round index". The round number is load-bearing throughout: `rounds/<n>/` paths (§2.3), the required `round` field on every record (§6.1), the triage idempotency key "(PR, round, record id, action)" (§7.3.1), and `rules.dead_after` rounds (§2.6.3.4). Under the deleted §9.3 the advance belonged to `cr recheck`; the scope cut removed the owner without appointing a replacement.
suggestion: State that `cr brief` increments the round index if and only if the current head differs from the head recorded in `meta.json`, that a same-head `cr brief` is idempotent with respect to the index, and that the first `cr brief` creates round 1.

finding: Nothing in the spec increments the round index. `round` is a required field on every record (§6.1), the key of every triage event (§7.3.1 keys by "(PR, round, record id, action)"), the directory name for `rounds/<n>/draft.md`, `rendered.json`, `posted.json`, and `summary.json` (§2.3), and a stored field on intent-gap entries (§4.1.3), rule-stats rows (§2.6.1.6), and waivers (§7.4.9). It is listed once as content of `meta.json` ("PR identity, issue key, profile id, active roles, round index") and never again. §9.3.3 says only "A new round MUST be started by re-running `cr brief` against the new head", but §3.7 also says `cr brief` "is safe to run at any point in a round" — so brief cannot unconditionally advance the counter, and no rule says it advances conditionally. An implementer cannot decide when `n` becomes `n+1`, which means `rounds/<n>/` paths and every idempotency key in §7.3.1 are unimplementable.
suggestion: State the rule explicitly in §9.3: `cr brief` MUST increment `meta.json`'s round index if and only if the current head differs from the head of the last recorded round (and MUST initialise it to 1 on first run), and MUST leave it unchanged otherwise. Say that all other commands read the index and never write it.

finding: Records abandoned by a head change can never leave a non-terminal state. §9.3.2 makes `cr` "refuse to draft, post, or probe" once the head moved, and §9.3.3 says "findings, units, cells, and probes MUST NOT" carry into the new round — but §9.1's table is declared exhaustive ("A transition not listed here MUST be rejected with exit code 4") and its only exits from `queued` are `cr draft` and `cr post --confirm`, precisely the two commands §9.3.2 forbids. The records therefore remain forever in `findings.ndjson` (§2.3: "All findings and questions, all states") in `draft`/`queued`, and §10.2.4's "No record remains in `draft` or `queued`" is not scoped to the round under evaluation, so the abandoned round's leftovers block completeness for every subsequent round too. §1.2.6 puts "Detecting that the head has moved, and declaring the recorded round stale" in scope, yet §9.1 defines no stale state and no transition that reaches one — the machinery that used to absorb this lived in the deleted re-review section.
suggestion: Add a terminal `stale` state to §9.1 with `draft`→`stale` and `queued`→`stale` produced when `cr brief` opens a round against a new head, and scope §10.2.4 to the records of the round being evaluated.

finding: The document's opening paragraph still promises the cut scope: "Delivers the complete reviewer-side loop for a single pull request: orient, review across four axes, prove findings with experiments, draft, human triage, post, and re-review until every thread is closed." §1.3.6 places "the re-review half of the loop" in v0.2 and §9 states "A record's life in v0.1 ends when it is posted." The abstract of a document that declares itself normative contradicts its own scope section, and it is the first thing an implementer reads.
suggestion: Rewrite the opening paragraph to end at posting, and name §1.2.6's stale-round detection as the boundary of v0.1.

finding: §10.1.5 requires `cr status` to report "Probes run, and probes that changed a finding's grade", but v0.1 has no re-grade path for the counter to observe. §6.2.1 computes the grade from the record's `citations` and referenced probe, §5.5.1 makes probe records "immutable once written", and §9.1's exhaustive table contains no transition that revisits a stored record — a record referencing a probe is graded `probed` at birth. The quantity is orphaned machinery from the multi-round design, where a later round could re-grade an existing finding.
suggestion: Replace it with a quantity computable from stored state, such as "probes run, probes referenced by a `probed` record, and probes referenced by no record".

finding: §10.2.4's condition and its gloss disagree about `duplicate`. The condition is "No record remains in `draft` or `queued`" but the gloss reads "every record has been posted, discarded, or suppressed", omitting `duplicate` — which §9.1 lists as a state and §9.1.2 names as terminal alongside the other three. A test writer taking the gloss as normative writes `TestCompleteness_DuplicateRecord_Incomplete`; one taking the condition writes the opposite assertion. Since §6.4.3 says suppressed duplicates "MUST be retained in state `duplicate`", any PR with an overlapping pair of findings hits this case.
suggestion: Amend the gloss to "every record has been posted, discarded, suppressed, or marked duplicate", or state the condition purely as the complement of §9.1.2's terminal set so the two can never drift.

finding: §11.1 enumerates what `--quiet` may never suppress — "The disabled and unavailable axes of §4.5.4, the probe cap of §5.6.4, the forcing counts of §6.3.2, the waiver and duplicate counts of §10.1.6, the sandbox recreation notice of §5.1.6, the stale-round report of §9.3.2, and the comment cap of §1.6.2" — and by being a closed enumeration it licenses suppressing every other qualifier. Two omissions have direct trust cost. §3.3.3 requires that on drift "`cr` MUST report for each claim whether its `span` still occurs in the new issue text"; suppressed, the reviewer reviews against a specification the tracker no longer states and posts findings citing superseded claims. §3.6.6 requires that "any coverage cell or record citing a retracted note MUST be reported as needing re-evaluation in the next round rather than silently retained"; suppressed, a record resting on hearsay the reviewer has explicitly withdrawn reaches the draft unmarked. §4.4.2's edge-case cap ("MUST report the cap when it binds") is a third.
suggestion: Add §3.3.3's claim-drift report, §3.6.6's retracted-note re-evaluation report, and §4.4.2's edge-case cap report to §11.1's list, and state the principle behind the list rather than only its members: `--quiet` MUST NOT suppress anything that qualifies a result `cr` is about to present as complete, current, or founded — so a disclosure added later inherits the protection instead of needing to be enumerated.

finding: §12.5 requires `--compact` to omit "ingested thread bodies" while protecting two other fields with a rationale that applies to thread bodies word for word: "It MUST NOT omit `evidence` or `citations`: the agent composes every posted body from them, and a compacted payload would leave the composition unfounded." The thread body is the only input to a judgement §2.1.3 reserves to the agent — "whether an existing human thread already covers a finding" — and the only basis for §3.5.4's suppression. A compacted `cr brief` or `cr review` payload therefore asks the agent to decide suppression from an author, an anchor, and a resolution state alone, and the failure mode is asymmetric: it does not suppress, and a second comment lands on a point a human reviewer already made. Under §1.6 that is a cost in itself, and it is the specific duplication cr exists to avoid.
suggestion: Move ingested thread bodies to the protected side of §12.5 alongside `evidence` and `citations`, or truncate rather than omit them and require the truncation to be disclosed in the payload. Leave `output_tail` and `input` compactable, since no §2.1.3 judgement rests on them, and state the governing principle: `--compact` may drop reproduction material, never the substrate of an agent judgement.

finding: §13.1 documents the loop as "brief, review fan-out, merge, record, probe, draft, human read, post". It names neither `cr map record` nor `cr cells record`, and omits the two-pass ordering of §4.6.5, under which `cr review <pr>` "MUST then refuse to emit prompts for the remaining axes until `mapping.ndjson` exists, with exit code 4". The skill is the agent's only instruction surface, so an agent following §13 as written hits an exit-4 wall with no documented remedy, and the mapping repair added in round 4 never reaches the party that has to produce it.
suggestion: Extend §13.1 to the full order — `cr brief` → `cr claims record` → `cr review --axis intent` → `cr map record` → `cr review` → `cr merge` → `cr record` → `cr cells record` → probe → draft → human read → post — and require §13 to name every command the agent must invoke.

finding: The new two-pass ordering leaves the intent pass self-referential and unchecked. §4.6.5 makes the intent role produce the mapping, yet the intent axis's own outputs are defined as functions of it: §4.1.2 "A unit mapped to zero claims MUST raise an unmapped-unit item" and §4.1.5 "`cr` MUST attach the issue key's notes to every unmapped unit" — which §4.6.1 requires every prompt to carry, in a pass where `cr` holds no mapping and cannot know which units are unmapped. Nothing then requires `cr map record` or `cr record` to cross-check the two artefacts, so a unit may be mapped to a claim in `mapping.ndjson` and simultaneously carry an unmapped-unit question, and no stated rule makes either wrong.
suggestion: State that during the intent pass `cr` attaches all issue-key notes to every unit (§4.1.5 being satisfied a fortiori), and require `cr record` to reject with exit code 1 an unmapped-unit item whose unit `mapping.ndjson` maps to at least one claim.

finding: §4.6.5's two-pass ordering makes one of pass 1's own requirements uncomputable. §4.1.5 says "`cr` MUST attach the issue key's notes to every unmapped unit", and §4.6.1 requires every emitted prompt to carry "the threads and notes of §3.5.3 and §4.1.5". But §4.6.5 states that `cr review <pr> --axis intent` "MUST emit prompts carrying the units and the claims but no mapping" — at that moment `mapping.ndjson` does not exist, so `cr` cannot know which units are unmapped and cannot apply §4.1.5's selection. Pass 2 is no help: the intent role, which is the one §4.1.5 exists to inform, has already run. An implementer must silently widen the rule to "attach notes to every unit" in pass 1, which is a different requirement from the one written.
suggestion: Restate §4.1.5 to match the pass structure: in the intent pass `cr` MUST attach the issue key's notes to every unit (the mapping does not yet exist), and after `cr map record` the unmapped set is what `cr status` and the coverage report use. Alternatively split the intent pass into a mapping-only prompt and a follow-up unmapped-unit prompt, and say which one carries the notes.

finding: §5.4.2 derives the gap probe's directory from a glob without defining the derivation: the test file goes "under `probe.test_dir` — defaulting to the root of the first entry in the profile's `tests.globs`". "Root" of a glob is undefined, and the natural entries make it matter: `tests/**/*Test.php` plausibly yields `tests`, but `**/*_test.go` or `*_spec.rb` have no literal prefix at all, so the default is either the sandbox root or an error and the spec picks neither. This is load-bearing beyond placement — §5.1.6's cleanliness check is defined as "no file under `probe.test_dir` whose name matches the probe naming scheme of §5.4.2", so two implementations disagreeing about the default disagree about whether a sandbox is clean.
suggestion: Define it mechanically: the default `probe.test_dir` is the longest leading path segment sequence of the first `tests.globs` entry that contains no `*`, `?`, or `[`; when that is empty the profile MUST declare `probe.test_dir` explicitly and `cr` MUST abort with exit code 3 naming the profile rather than defaulting to the sandbox root.

finding: Dedup is assigned to two commands. §6.5.1 requires `cr merge` to "merge per-role NDJSON files, apply §6.4", and §6.4.3 within it says "Suppressed duplicates MUST be retained in state `duplicate` with `duplicate_of` naming the representative" — a state assignment. §9.1 then says the opposite: "`cr merge` is not a producer: it runs on role output files before any record exists, and §6.4.3 marks duplicates as `cr record` writes them." An implementer cannot tell whether the merged file carries `state`/`duplicate_of`, nor whether `cr record` re-runs §6.4.1 against records already in `findings.ndjson` from an earlier `cr record` in the same round.
suggestion: Split the responsibility explicitly: `cr merge` computes the grouping and writes `duplicate_of` on its output file; `cr record` is the only writer of `state`. State whether `cr record` re-applies §6.4.1 against previously stored records of the same round.

finding: §7.2's marker table requires an event that §7.3.1's closed vocabulary cannot name. The table says of `severity`: "Freely editable; recorded as a triage event". §7.3.1 keys triage events by `(PR, round, record id, action)` and closes the action set — "drawn from `kept`, `softened`, `discarded-not-here`, and `discarded-wrong`" plus `raised`, and "These five action names are the complete vocabulary the statistics below are computed from." There is no action for a severity change, and the idempotency key requires one. An implementer either invents a sixth name, contradicting "complete vocabulary" and polluting the §7.3.3 denominator, or silently drops the event the §7.2 table mandates. `TestTriage_SeverityEdit_WritesEvent` has no expected value.
suggestion: Either add `reseverity` (or `severity-changed`) as a sixth action name in §7.3.1, stating explicitly that it is excluded from the §7.3.3 demotion rate, or delete "recorded as a triage event" from the `severity` row of §7.2 and say severity edits are carried on the record only.

finding: §9.3.1 requires the head comparison "on every command that reads per-PR state". That sweeps in `cr status`, `cr context`, `cr answer`, `cr waivers list --pr`, and `cr stats`, each of which would need a live `gh` call to learn the current head. It contradicts §2.1.1 ("Every `cr` command MUST be reproducible given the same state directory, the same head SHA, and the same inputs"), makes read-only inspection fail without network access, and specifies no behaviour for a head lookup that itself fails.
suggestion: Restrict the mandatory comparison to the commands §9.3.2 gates (`cr draft`, `cr post`, `cr probe run`, `cr test`) plus `cr brief` and `cr status`; for the rest, report the recorded head and specify that a failed head lookup is reported, not fatal.

finding: §10.2.4 reads "No record remains in `draft` or `queued`: every record has been posted, discarded, or suppressed." The gloss omits `duplicate`, which §9.1.2 lists as terminal alongside the other three ("Terminal states are `posted`, `discarded`, `duplicate`, and `suppressed`"). A round containing a deduplicated record satisfies the first clause and fails the second as literally written.
suggestion: Add `duplicate` to the enumeration, or delete the gloss and let the first clause stand alone.
